Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Extended-history summarization: qualification & next steps (post-demo)

Claire — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

What you told us (summary)
- Use case: clinicians need a single-note summary that preserves decision points from across a patient’s multi-year chart (lab events, meds, consult notes).
- Volume: ~1.5M notes/year across 300k patients; typical doc cluster per patient ~8–25 docs, median total tokens per patient ~45k.
- Latency expectation: interactive clinician-facing summary ~500–900ms for the final aggregation call; async batch summaries tolerated up to 60s.
- Data posture: PHI, must remain in VPC; audit logs and KMS required.

Call takeaways re: model fit and risks
- We validated that naive truncation will lose salient context (concern for longitudinal decision history).
- They prefer extractive+abstractive hybrid summaries to preserve timestamps and decisions.
- Quality regression tolerance: very low — summaries must not hallucinate medication changes.

What I’m proposing next
1) Baseline eval: run 3 model families (Llama-4x-12B-32k-Quant, RedGem-7B-16k, RedGem-13B-32k-FA) on a small set of 50 representative patient histories to compare fidelity and truncation behavior. Attached: prompt_set_extended_v1.jsonl (50 prompts + golden summaries).
2) Benchmarks: we’ll produce ROUGE/ROUGE-Long, faithfulness checks (fact-extraction pass), and a hallucination classifier score. Preliminary bench will live here: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/long-context-evals/NW-0043
3) Privacy/ops: propose Private deployment (VPC) with KMS; include SOC2 evidence in the next attach pack.

Next steps / asks
- Claire: please confirm the 50 patient examples (I’ll accept a redacted export or a small S3 drop).
- Internal: Neha/Rishi/Marissa — can you review the prompts/bench plan and aim to have an initial run by EOD Friday (Dec 4)?

Attachments: prompt_set_extended_v1.jsonl (prompt + golden), longdoc_bench_summary_20261202.csv (empty skeleton), call_recording_20261202.mp3 (call audio stub).

Thanks — Ben

--

Subject: Re: Extended-history summarization: qualification & next steps (post-demo)

Ben — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide the 50 patient examples as de-identified exports; I’ll have our engineering lead drop a gzipped ndjson to the S3 bucket you gave during the call. Expected delivery: tomorrow morning (Dec 3).
- Regarding latency: the 500–900ms target is for the UI-side interactive call after we've precomputed embeddings/prefix caches. If the model requires stitching multiple windows, we need to know expected server-side latencies for worst-case patients (70–90k tokens).
- On hallucination tolerance: we have a safety team that will run a manual review on a random 10% sample. Any automated hallucination metric you run should prioritize omitted-critical-fact penalties over small phrasing differences.

Also, on models — you mentioned RedGem variants and Llama-4x-32k. Can you include cost-per-1k-token estimates for the baseline runs? That’ll feed into our ROI calc.

— Claire

Claire Huang

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 19:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Extended-history summarization: qualification & next steps (post-demo)

Claire — perfect, thanks. Quick follow-up inline and with the benchmarking/cost notes attached below.

On latency: good call — we’ll treat precomputed prefix caching as the primary optimization. For worst-case stitching we’ll log both end-to-end and per-window times. I’ll include 95p/99p tail estimates once we have the benchmark run.

Models & rough cost (baseline run estimates for the 50-patient set)
- Llama-4x-32k (float16) — expected best-in-class fidelity on long windows; estimated compute $0.28 / 1k tokens (baseline with dynamic-kernel path).
- RedGem-13B-32k-FA (quant) — lower cost, competitive abstractive quality with better batch packing; est $0.11 / 1k tokens.
- RedGem-7B-16k (quant) — fastest latency on smaller windows; est $0.06 / 1k tokens.

Why these three: Llama-4x gives us a ceiling on factuality across long context; RedGem-13B-FA is our likely production sweet spot for cost vs fidelity; 7B is for a constrained-latency hybrid approach (extract-first, then abstractive condense).

Bench links & artifacts (will populate after runs)
- Preliminary bench report (skeleton): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/long-context-evals/NW-0043#report
- Prompt set (attached): prompt_set_extended_v1.jsonl — includes two prompt families:
  * extractive scaffolding prompts (fact-extract then condense)
  * single-pass abstractive prompts with block markers and temporal pointers

Next steps / asks (short)
- Claire: confirm S3 drop and share the object key when ready.
- Safety/ops ask: we’ll need a short MOU for data handling in the Private deployment; I can share our standard one-page MOU.
- Internal: Neha/Rishi — can you run the baseline pipeline (50 patients) and share the longdoc_bench_summary_20261202.csv + per-model logs by EOD Friday (Dec 4)? If any of the models require GPU variants we don’t have on the private cluster, flag ASAP and we’ll schedule Dedicated capacity.

Thanks — Ben

Attachments: prompt_set_extended_v1.jsonl

Subject: INTERNAL: Run baseline evals for NoteWell (50 patients) — priority

Team — moving this to the internal thread so we can coordinate execution. Copy of Claire’s asks above included below for context. Summary of what I need from each of you: 

What to run
- Dataset: prompt_set_extended_v1.jsonl (50 patient-level prompts + golds) — in Drive folder NW-0043.
- Models: Llama-4x-32k (float16), RedGem-13B-32k-FA (quant), RedGem-7B-16k (quant).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L (full), ROUGE-Long, fact-extraction F1 (tool provided in eval harness), hallucination-score (binary classifier + omission penalty).

Rough timeline (EOD Fri, Dec 4)
- Neha: kick off runs, ensure prefix caching is enabled for models that support it; collect per-request latency (p50/p95/p99) and token counts.
- Rishi: implement the fact-extraction pass and hallucination classifier on the outputs; return a sample-level matrix (50 rows x metrics).
- Marissa: prepare the longdoc_bench_summary_20261202.csv and populate the dashboard link (I’ll create the initial tab).

Known risks / guidance
- Watch for truncation artifacts when sequence >32k; record the step where model had to window/strip context.
- For Llama-4x runs, add a control run where we do blockwise chain-of-thought-style extraction to see if staged extraction reduces hallucination.

Deliverables (Friday EOD)
- longdoc_bench_summary_20261202.csv (populated)
- per-model logs (s3 paths)
- short writeup of any fidelity regressions or hallucination patterns (bullet list)

If any infra or Dedicated/GPU questions pop up, ping me and I’ll escalate with Solutions Ops. Thanks — please ack in-thread with ETA.

--
